source.title: Spectrally-normalized margin bounds for neural networks
source.authors: P. Bartlett; Dylan J. Foster; Matus Telgarsky

record.tranche_reason: The paper trains AlexNet with original and randomized CIFAR-10 labels using SGD and reports training-error and excess-risk results, directly testing random-label fitting.
record.gate_note: Figure-only values are not reconstructed. The paper also compares Lipschitz constants and margin distributions, but those measures do not themselves establish the claim’s specific training-error and test-at-chance outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study independently trains an AlexNet-like network with SGD on true and randomized CIFAR-10 labels. Figure 1 explicitly marks zero training error, and Section 2 states that architecture and learning rate were unchanged across experiments.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors present a margin-based generalization bound and report that Lipschitz constants correlate with excess risk, while margin normalization neutralizes their growth during training. Normalized margins distinguish randomized-label tasks from true-label tasks, and tested weight decay does not visibly improve these margins.
record.recipe_differences: Uses vanilla SGD and an AlexNet-like architecture on standard datasets with randomized labels; the paper’s focus is margin-based generalization bounds, and it does not report optimization-time comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The text says the architecture and settings were unchanged across experiments; margin distributions vary by dataset and label condition. Figure 4b reports varying L2 regularization for CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized margin distributions distinguish true labels from random labels on CIFAR-10 and MNIST and place Gaussian inputs below randomized-label CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectrally normalized training margins distinguish these learning tasks by the authors' measure of difficulty.

fits_no_version.finding: Varying weight decay produces no visible improvement in CIFAR-10 normalized margin distributions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested weight-decay settings do not visibly improve normalized margins; this alone does not establish V5's fitting or generalization outcomes.

record.problems: Relevant numerical results are shown only in figures; the text does not state test error at chance for random labels or exact epochs for zero training error.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 Lipschitz-constant curves and Figures 2–4 margin-distribution results were not extracted as claim-version rows because those measures do not establish the named training-error and test-at-chance outcomes. V3 and V5 were tested but no qualifying row was retained.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error is not established in the supplied text.
No readable comparison of time to fit true versus random labels, and no corruption-fraction timing sweep.
Zero training error on Gaussian inputs is not established; shuffled and independently permuted pixels are not investigated.
No sweep of label-corruption fractions measuring both perfect training fit and test-error degradation.

No direct result establishes fitting random labels under explicit regularization or quantifies true-label generalization with versus without it. Weight-decay margin comparisons do not establish these outcomes; dropout and augmentation are not separately tested.
No measurement establishes that real patterns are learned before noisy labels are memorized.

record.verdict_notes: The record overstates V3 and V5 as tested versions: their reported margin comparisons measure related constructs. The supplied figure text does not permit reliable numerical reconstruction of convergence epochs or test error. Omitted margin and complexity results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The text identifies the earliest zero-training-error epoch for CIFAR-10 with random labels, but does not state that test error is at chance.
The paper compares margin distributions for Gaussian random inputs and random labels, but does not state that Gaussian inputs reach zero training error.

The paper reports that L2 regularization does not visibly improve margin distributions, but does not test whether regularization prevents fitting random labels or whether removing it harms true-label generalization.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD on CIFAR-10 with random labels; figure marks the earliest epoch with zero training error.
rows.note: The caption says the x marks the earliest epoch with zero training error; no epoch value is stated in the text.
rows.check: The training-error value is explicitly zero in the caption; only the epoch is unreadable. Specify the AlexNet-like architecture with normalization and regularization removed, and vanilla SGD with learning rate 0.01. Chance-level test error is not established by the supplied text.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD on CIFAR-10 with original labels; figure reports excess risk across epochs.
rows.measure: Excess risk (test error minus training error)
rows.note: The text says excess risk is plotted, but supplies no values or explicit description of true-label test performance.
rows.check: True-label excess risk is a contextual control, not a measurement of random-label fitting. The supplied text provides neither a readable value nor enough information to establish good true-label generalization without regularization.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared normalized margin distributions after replacing CIFAR-10 images with Gaussian random images matching first- and second-order image statistics.

conditions.value: CIFAR-10 images replaced by Gaussian random images matching first- and second-order image statistics

rows.note: The text says random inputs are harder than random labels; the figure-only margin result does not establish zero training error.
rows.check: The normalized margin comparison does not establish zero training error on Gaussian inputs. Retain this finding as contextual evidence under fits_no_version rather than a V3 outcome.

relationships.condition: AlexNet-like network on randomized CIFAR-10 labels, vanilla SGD at learning rate 0.01, without explicit regularization
relationships.reason: R1 explicitly reaches zero training error; Section 2 confirms unchanged architecture and learning rate across experiments. This supports the fitting component.
relationships.display_finding: Training error reached zero with the same architecture and learning rate across experiments.
